_README: Differences from real S3 that this server accepts, with the reason each is
accepted. Anything NOT listed here fails `s3probe.py diff --strict`, which
is what the `aws_compat` integration test runs.
A rule matches a finding when `op` equals the operation name (or "*"),
`kind` equals the finding kind, and `contains` appears in the detail text.
Adding a rule is a deliberate act: it says 'we know, and here is why'.

rules.why: AWS request-tracing header. Carries no protocol meaning; clients log it at most.
AWS advertises 'AmazonS3'. Impersonating that would be worse than differing.
S3 encrypts at rest by default and says so. This server has no SSE.
Region discovery. This server is regionless; see the get_bucket_location note.
ARNs are an AWS-account concept with no local equivalent.
S3 Access Points are an AWS feature; there is nothing to report.
Additional checksums (CRC32/CRC32C/SHA1/SHA256/CRC64NVME) are not implemented. See ChecksumAlgorithm below.
Response framing. AWS chunks some XML replies where we send a length, and vice versa; both are valid HTTP and no client can tell the difference.

AWS is inconsistent about this and we are not. It sends application/xml on ListObjects, CompleteMultipartUpload and every error, omits it entirely on CreateMultipartUpload and GetObjectAttributes, and sends it on a bodiless HeadBucket. We send it on every XML body and nothing else. Reproducing the inconsistency would need a per-operation table serving no client: SDKs dispatch on the operation they invoked, never on this header.

AWS now adds a default CRC64NVME checksum to every upload and reports the algorithm in listings. This server stores no additional checksums, so it reports none -- the same shape AWS produced before that default existed.

AWS reports the bucket's region; this server has no region concept, so it returns the empty LocationConstraint that S3 itself uses to mean us-east-1. A client that treats empty as us-east-1 -- which every SDK does -- works unchanged.

Deliberate superset. AWS returns the per-part list only for uploads made with a COMPOSITE checksum, and returns a bare PartsCount otherwise. Every multipart object here has a composite ETag built from per-part MD5s -- structurally AWS's COMPOSITE case -- and withholding the boundaries would leave callers a PartsCount they cannot use. See handlers/get_object_attributes.
